request.spec:
A search box and a button list, over this sheet and every other sheet of its tree, every person
whose name or an alias contains the typed text (case ignored), one line per person as
<sheet id> <name> <due-total>, this sheet's people first in list order, then the other sheets' by
sheet id.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A search box and a button list, over this sheet and every other sheet of its tree, every person
whose name or an alias contains the typed text (case ignored), one line per person as
<sheet id> <name> <due-total>, this sheet's people first in list order, then the other sheets' by
sheet id.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The tree search is in, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**How it works**
- **Server:** a new endpoint at `GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/tree-search?text=…` (`src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/rollup/TreeSearchController.java`).
  - It searches the sheet's whole tree: its topmost ancestor and every sheet below that.
  - The current sheet comes first, then the other sheets sorted by id. Within each sheet, people appear in list order.
  - A person matches if their name or any alias contains the typed text, ignoring case. An empty search lists everyone.
  - Each line is `<sheet id> <name> <due-total>`, with the due-total each sheet already works out for that person, or `n/a` when there isn't one. People merged into someone else are left out, as they are everywhere else.
- **Front end:** a new "Search the tree" section (`src/main/frontend/src/app/features/tree-search/tree-search.ts`) sits on the main screen above the Audit section. I built it the same way as the existing audit viewer, with the test ids `search-name`, `search`, `search-count`, `search-line` and `search-error`. Each press clears the old count and results before the new ones arrive, and loading another sheet clears them too.

Retired people are still listed, with the due-total their sheet shows for them, even when "show retired" is off.

The search doesn't change anything, so it writes nothing to the audit file. The spec doesn't expect any audit lines from it either.

probe.probe_text:
I didn't change anything. Below is what the code currently does, using the code's own names.

# 1. Figures and the rules behind them

## Per claim (`claims.ts` template, `Claim.java`)

| Shown (`data-testid`) | Where it comes from |
|---|---|
| `claim-number` | Given when the claim is opened (`ClaimService.number`). By default it is `FY<year>-<n>`: the next number in the fiscal year its **due-by** falls in (`Sheet.fiscalStartMonth`), counted across the whole sheet tree (`nextFiscalNumberInTree`). While the sheet numbers by period (`periodNumberingFrom`) it is `<period>-<n>`, or `X-<n>` when the due-by is in no period. A void claim keeps its number. A redate (moving to another period), a reassign or a transfer gives a new number, and the old one is retired (`retireNumberWithin`) and never reused. A DRAFT has no number. |
| `claim-amount` | As typed. With lines, it is the sum of qty × unit (`Claim.addLine`), and an edit to any other amount is refused (`ClaimLinedAmountException`). A negative amount makes it a **correction** (`isCorrection`). |
| `claim-date` | As given. If blank on add: `entryDate` if set, else the sheet's today (`dateOrEntryDate`). If blank on edit: today. |
| `claim-due-by` | **Fixed when the claim is added**: the `terms`-th business day after its date (`HolidayService.businessDaysAfter`, which skips weekends and holidays). Terms come from `termsOf`: the person's own `terms`, else the grade's terms in force on the claim date, else the sheet's (`START_TERMS = 14`). It never moves when the date or the terms change. It is fixed again only when a holiday is added, for claims not SETTLED/VOID whose due-by is on or after that holiday. |
| `claim-due` | `claimDueCents` (front end) / `chargedFigureOf` (server). See below. |
| `claim-status` | `ClaimStatus.canBecome`: DRAFT→OPEN→SETTLED. DRAFT, OPEN or PENDING can go to VOID. DRAFT can go to DELETED. A clerk's settle above the limit gives PENDING instead. PENDING goes to SETTLED by `approve` or back to OPEN by `reject`. |
| `claim-overdue` | `isOverdue`: OPEN or PENDING, not deferred, and `dueBy + grace(grade on claim date)` is before today. |
| `claim-deferred` / `-until` | `isDeferred`: OPEN and today is before `deferredUntil`. The display flag ignores status, so a voided claim still shows as deferred. |
| `claim-stated` | `stated`. `isBound` means stated **and not PENDING**. |
| `claim-period` | The period that contains the **due-by**, not the claim date. |
| `claim-late-entry` | Set on add or split when the due-by falls in a soft-closed period (`softClosedOn`). |
| `claim-opened-by`, `-proofs`, `-corrects`, `-split-from`, `-reminded`, `-batch`, log/comments/lines | Stored as recorded. Each log line keeps the due at that moment. |

### How a claim's due is worked out (`figureOf` → `charged` → `floored`, mirrored in `claimDueCents`)
1. If `settledDue` is set, show it. It is frozen and has no floor or new charge.
2. Otherwise the **figure** is `statedDue` if the claim is bound, else amount × rate%. The rate is the one for the person's grade *on the claim date* (`gradeOn`), using the rate in force on the claim date (`RateLevels`/`InheritedRates`). If the sheet has none, it falls back to its ancestors, up to three levels. If there is no rate at all, the due is `n/a`.
3. Add the **late charge** (`LateCharge`). For each full 30-day boundary past `dueBy + grace`, the charge is the late % in force on that boundary date, applied to figure + earlier charges (it compounds), rounded each step. A boundary at 0.00% adds nothing. A statement never binds the charge.
4. Take the greater of that and the **floor** in force on the claim date (`START_FLOOR = 1.00`). Corrections get no floor and no charge.
5. **Rounding** (`Rounding`) is HALF_UP when the basis date is before `policyDate` (blank means today), otherwise HALF_EVEN. A correction rounds by the date of the claim it corrects.

## Per person (`people.ts`; audit copy in `RollupService`)
- **`person-claimed`**: the sum of the amounts of claims that count, leaving out corrections.
- **Which claims count** (`Person.counts` / `countsFor`): status OPEN, PENDING or SETTLED, minus:
  - deferred claims;
  - open claims that are neither bound nor kept out by the person. "Kept out" (`keptOut`) means the claim is dated within a **hold**, or the person's retirement date has been reached on today.
- **`person-due-total`**: the sum of the dues of counting claims, then capped at the sheet's `cap` (`Sheet.capped`).
  - It shows **n/a** when the grade the person has today has no rate today **and** no counting claim is "fixed". A claim is fixed if it has a settled or stated due, or a due under a different grade than today's, or under a rate not in force today.
- **`person-excess`**: how far the uncapped total is above the cap (0.00 otherwise).
- **`person-overdue-count` / `-overdue-total`**: counting claims that are overdue, and their dues.
- **`person-settled-total` / `person-open-total`**: the uncapped total split into SETTLED and open claims.
- **`person-aged-0-30 / 31-60 / 61`**: dues of open counting claims, bucketed by days from the claim date to today.
- **`person-period-<name>-due-total`**:
  - If the period is closed or soft-closed: the figure fixed at close (`closedPersonDues`).
  - Otherwise: live dues of claims whose due-by is in the period, counted by the status they had at the period's end (`countsAt` / `statusAt`).
- **`person-statement-count` / `-stated-total` / `-statement-date`** (`StatementService`): taking a statement records the person's due-total *with* charges, capped. It then binds each counting claim to its figure *without* the charge, and unbinds the rest. As-of statements (`bindAsOf`) replay statuses, bindings, holds, grades, rates and settings as they were recorded by that date. A steward can cancel the last statement, which unbinds everything (`cancelLast`).
- **`person-backing`**: for each patron, their SETTLED frozen dues dated within the last 90 days × their share ÷ 100. Shares are 100 split equally, rounded half to even, with the remainder going to the first patron named.
- **`person-cut-total`**: pool cuts (`PoolService`). A pot is split by share; retired members, members on hold today, or members out of their dates get 0.00; the remainder goes to the smallest non-zero cut.
- **`person-active`** (`activeOn`): has an open counting claim dated within the last 30 days.
- Other row fields:
  - `person-grade` is the grade in force on today;
  - `person-retired` / `person-retired-from`, `held`, `clashing` (`clashingIds`: the name or an alias is used on another sheet in the tree), and snapshot lines (written when today changes).

## Sheet totals
- **Rollup claimed-total**: not trimmed.
- **Header and rollup due-total and overdue-total**: these use `trimmedSum`. With three or more figures, the single highest and single lowest person are dropped. An n/a due-total is not a figure.
- **Settled, open and cut totals**: plain sums.
- **By grade** leaves out retired people. **By tag** counts a claim once if it or its person carries the tag. **By month** uses the claim date. **By period** shows a change versus the previous period. There are also counts by status and by void reason.
- **Consolidated** totals add in the sheet's descendants.

## Who may do what
- **Roles** (`SettingService.roleOf`): CLERK by default. A user acts as STEWARD while a steward's delegation covers today.
  - A VIEWER is refused every write (`ViewerGuard`).
  - An archived sheet refuses every write (`ArchivedGuard`).
  - An as-of view refuses changes (`AsOfGuard`).
- **Permission matrix** (`mayDo`; standing rules in `STANDING_PERMISSIONS`): open, settle, void and close are clerk or steward; reassign and reopen are steward only. The sheet can override these per action.
- **Steward only**: approve or reject PENDING, resettle, redate, void a SETTLED claim (only within `VOID_SETTLED_DAYS = 7` of settling), merge, transfer, cancel a statement.
- **Settle**:
  - Refused for the person who opened or last edited the claim (`isOpenedOrEditedBy`), and for a deferred claim.
  - If a clerk settles and the due is above `clerkLimit` (as in force today), the claim goes to PENDING instead.
  - Settle and approve are refused when the claim has no proofs and its due is above `proofThreshold`. That threshold is the grade's or the sheet's, in force on the claim date.
- **Open**:
  - Refused when the note is empty and the due is above `noteThreshold`.
  - Refused when the person already has `period.cap` OPEN or PENDING claims due in that period (`refuseOverCap`).
- **Edit**: only a DRAFT can be edited, and not while another user's editor lock is on it (`lockedBy`).
- **Delete and restore**: a DRAFT can be deleted. It can be restored only on the same sheet today it was deleted.
- **Corrections**: a correction must name a SETTLED claim of the same person (`refuseUnlessCorrects`). Only a correction may name one.
- **Retirement** (`mayClaimOn`): no claim may be dated after the retirement date, or inside a past retirement.
- **Refs**: a reference is unique per sheet, ignoring case.

## Closed periods, holds, imports and today
- **Closed period** (`refuseIfClosed`): any claim whose **due-by** is inside a closed period cannot be added, edited, opened, settled, resettled, voided, deleted, restored, deferred, proofed, lined, moved, split or redated. Closing fixes each person's period due-total and the period's total. Soft-close fixes the figures but still allows changes. Reopening (subject to permission) makes the figures live again. When today changes, open periods whose to-date plus `graceDays` is before today are closed automatically.
- **Hold**: an open, unbound claim dated within the hold leaves every live total. Pool cuts look at holds *in force today* instead.
- **Imports**: all of these are one change each, so a single bad line refuses the whole thing.
  - People import (name, grade, terms, contact): a matching name or alias edits that person, with the grade recorded from today; anything else adds a person.
  - Rate import: sets each rate as the rate form would.
  - Claim paste (name, amount, date, note, with `#ref`): adds DRAFTs as the claim form would.
  - Quick-add: creates a grade-A person when no name or alias matches.
  - Plan generate: makes the missing DRAFTs up to today; each one goes through on its own.
- **Bulk actions**: each claim goes through on its own, in list order, except bulk settle, which is all-or-nothing and gets a batch number.
- **Changing today**: writes a SNAPSHOT line per person, runs the auto-close, and releases every editor lock.
- **Audit**: a change writes ROLLUP and TOTALS lines when the figures move, and an ALERT line when a person's due-total crosses `alertThreshold`.

# 2. How hard it was to follow

It is scattered and tangled. The due/count/n/a rules are written out at least four times: the screen's own TypeScript (`claims.ts`, `people.ts`) and three separate Java copies in `ClaimService`, `RollupService` and `StatementService`. Each copy compares slightly differently (by rate id, by Optional equality, or by object identity), and permissions and date guards are re-checked by hand in every service method. A new developer would struggle to find the single source of truth, because there isn't one; the long doc comments are the most reliable map.
